newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market steady, liquidity to tighten.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market steady, liquidity to tighten.

text.p: Croatian money market rates were steady to lower on abundant supply of kuna on Thursday, but dealers expected liquidity to tighten in the coming days.
They said bank accounts, which are thinner already compared to the past week, would probably empty after Friday's payment of monthly tax by their clients.
Banks also have to pay kuna to the central bank for the purchase of some 36 million German marks on Wednesday. Next week was seen as even more problematic due to pension payments.
"Some lenders were already withdrawing their placements today, but others banks repaid old loans so we managed to square the lot," said one dealer.
All of the morning's 21.8 million kuna demand was fully met. Call money funds were granted mostly at 10.5 percent, though price for one large bank was cut to 10 percent.
Two-week and 30-day interbank rates were also flat at 13 and 15 percent respectively.

Wednesday's overnight trade totalled a meagre 2.9 million kuna as only one bank had shortfall. Overnight deals are made at one percentage point below the daily average. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
